speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chest skin lesion; please describe its color, size, shape, and if you have noticed any changes, pain, or bleeding.

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details, Mr. 63. You mentioned the lesion is growing over two months without pain or itching, and you have a history of diabetes. Is the lesion raised above the skin surface, and does it have an irregular border or varied colors? Also, do you smoke or have a history of significant sun exposure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of diabetes and a growing, painless chest lesion with irregular borders, I am concerned about a potential skin malignancy. Has this lesion bled or ulcerated at any point? REQUEST TEST: Skin_biopsy_of_chest_lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_skin_lesion_photo.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology findings confirm the presence of atypical melanocytes infiltrating the epidermis and dermis, consistent with a diagnosis of malignant melanoma. The lesion presents as a firm, partly elevated area on the chest exhibiting asymmetry, irregular borders, and varied coloration with a diameter exceeding 6mm. No bleeding or ulceration was reported by the patient.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignant Melanoma. The histopathology confirms atypical melanocytes with asymmetry, irregular borders, varied colors, and a diameter over 6mm, consistent with this diagnosis. Please ensure you have a referral for immediate excision and staging.
